symptom: Python jsonschema Draft 2020-12 accepts a synthetic trailing LF after a 64-hex sourceRowDigest and after a timestamp matched by the Runtime Decision Ledger exactInstant pattern because dollar can match before a final newline. The Node runtime rejects the corresponding noncanonical values. This is a schema-only cross-engine lexical mismatch, not an observed private record or production incident.
lesson: JSON Schema regex dollar anchors are not portable exact-end assertions: Python re.search admits a final LF that the JavaScript runtime rejects. Schema-only consumers must not treat lexical acceptance as authenticated timing or digest evidence.
guardrail: Use (?![\\s\\S]) as the strict terminal assertion for K1 exactInstant and sourceRowDigest schema patterns. Keep runtime timestamp parsing and digest checks authoritative; retain LF, CRLF, Unicode terminator and valid-control tests. Reuse the Shadow Evidence terminal-boundary guardrail without changing Current BUY or production.
